edge.fromTitle: Tell what kind of text you are looking at
edge.toTitle: Place a source in time and place

from.title: Tell what kind of text you are looking at
from.statement: You can say whether a source is Torah, Mishnah, Gemara, commentary, a code, or a prayer.
from.transferKp: Label the genre of a snippet from a genre not shown in the lesson.

to.title: Place a source in time and place
to.statement: You can place a source in a rough time and place.
to.introduceKp: Attach every source to a rough era and setting before drawing conclusions from it.

proposals.authoringGuidance: Name the single reading move a learner needs after "You can say whether a source is Torah, Mishnah, Gemara, commentary, a code, or a prayer." to be ready for "You can place a source in a rough time and place." — which begins by "Attach every source to a rough era and setting before drawing conclusions from it.". If the jump is genuinely one move, reject this and keep the direct edge.
proposals.note: A 6-layer jump may need more than one intermediate; this proposes one at layer 4. After authoring it, re-run to decompose the two shorter edges it leaves.

from.title: Tell primary text from commentary
from.statement: You can separate a primary text from a comment written about it.
from.transferKp: Separate text from commentary on a halakhic page you have not seen.

to.title: Make a scaffolded first pass
to.statement: You can make a supported first pass through an unfamiliar short source.
to.introduceKp: Walk the source once for shape, once for signals, once for sense, with support ready at each pass.

from.title: Name what is uncertain
from.statement: You can name the point of uncertainty or dispute at the heart of a case.
from.transferKp: Find the uncertainty in an unseen halakhic case.

to.title: Ask a good question
to.statement: You can ask a clear, answerable question about a source.
to.introduceKp: Turn a vague 'I don't get it' into a question with a shape that could actually be answered.

from.statement: You can recognize when a source leaves a tension unresolved on purpose.
from.transferKp: Judge resolution in an unseen aggadic or narrative passage.

edge.fromTitle: Distinguish a ruling from a discussion
edge.toTitle: Let the genre set your expectations

from.title: Distinguish a ruling from a discussion
from.statement: You can tell a settled ruling from open discussion around it.
from.transferKp: Make the same call on an unseen halakhic paragraph.

to.title: Let the genre set your expectations
to.statement: You can use a source's genre to decide how it should and should not be read.
to.introduceKp: Match the reading stance to the genre: a poem invites resonance, a code invites precision.

from.title: Follow the response
from.statement: You can follow how a response answers, narrows, or reframes an objection.
from.transferKp: Trace a response in an unseen sugya.

to.title: Make a scaffolded first pass
to.statement: You can make a supported first pass through an unfamiliar short source.
to.introduceKp: Walk the source once for shape, once for signals, once for sense, with support ready at each pass.

from.title: Recognize argument connectors
from.statement: You can recognize the small words that mean 'therefore', 'but', 'as it says', and 'this teaches'.
from.transferKp: Trace the connectors through a Mussar passage you have not seen.

to.title: Mark an objection
to.statement: You can mark an objection and describe the pressure it puts on a claim.
to.introduceKp: When the text pushes back, name what exactly it threatens: the claim, its reason, or its scope.

edge.fromTitle: Notice where a translation makes a choice
edge.toTitle: Weigh a translation against the original

from.title: Notice where a translation makes a choice
from.statement: You can see where a translation adds, drops, or chooses a meaning the original leaves open.
from.transferKp: Find a translation choice in a piece of Jewish thought you have not studied.

to.title: Weigh a translation against the original
to.statement: You can judge what a translation's choice does to the meaning by holding it against the original word.
to.introduceKp: Set the translation beside the original word; name what the translation committed to, and what it left behind.

proposals.authoringGuidance: Name the single reading move a learner needs after "You can see where a translation adds, drops, or chooses a meaning the original leaves open." to be ready for "You can judge what a translation's choice does to the meaning by holding it against the original word." — which begins by "Set the translation beside the original word; name what the translation committed to, and what it left behind.". If the jump is genuinely one move, reject this and keep the direct edge.

edge.toTitle: Ask who made it and for whom

from.title: Identify who acts
from.statement: You can name who is acting in a case and what they do.
from.transferKp: Do the same for an unseen narrative from history material.

to.title: Ask who made it and for whom
to.statement: You can ask who produced a source and which community it addressed.
to.introduceKp: Name the author and intended audience; a text written for scholars reads differently than one for a congregation.

proposals.authoringGuidance: Name the single reading move a learner needs after "You can name who is acting in a case and what they do." to be ready for "You can ask who produced a source and which community it addressed." — which begins by "Name the author and intended audience; a text written for scholars reads differently than one for a congregation.". edge.toTitle: Name the limits of what you learned

from.title: Recognize an open tension
from.statement: You can recognize when a source leaves a tension unresolved on purpose.
from.transferKp: Judge resolution in an unseen aggadic or narrative passage.

to.title: Name the limits of what you learned
to.statement: You can name the boundaries of what your reading has and has not established.
to.introduceKp: End each study with a sentence beginning 'What I have not settled is...'.

edge.fromTitle: Weigh a translation against the original
edge.toTitle: Use translation to check, not to skip

from.title: Weigh a translation against the original
from.statement: You can judge what a translation's choice does to the meaning by holding it against the original word.
from.transferKp: Weigh a translation choice against the original in an unseen source, and say what rides on it.

to.title: Use translation to check, not to skip
to.statement: You can use a translation to verify your reading rather than to replace it.
to.introduceKp: Commit to a read first, then open the translation only to confirm or correct it.

edge.toTitle: Carry a reading move across genres

from.title: Find the shared question
from.statement: You can find the common question that two sources are both answering.
from.transferKp: Find the shared question across two unseen sources.

to.title: Carry a reading move across genres
to.statement: You can apply a reading move in a genre you never practiced it in.
to.introduceKp: Take a move you own in one genre and run it, out loud, in a genre that feels unrelated.
